# Paravitāraṇakathā (Kv 2.4)

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Paravitāraṇakathā* (Kv 2.4) is the fourth debate of the second chapter (*vagga*) of the Abhidhamma treatise *Kathāvatthu* [SuttaCentral]. It examines the thesis *atthi arahato paravitāraṇā* ("an arahant can be guided or instructed by others"), which corresponds to the fourth proposition of the celebrated "Five Points" attributed in early sectarian traditions to Mahādeva [Williams 2000; Skorupski 1991; Dutt 1978]. In this debate, opposing schools maintained that an arahant might acquire knowledge or develop faith through the instruction and guidance of a preceptor rather than entirely on their own, drawing distinctions between types of arahants [Dutt 1978; Dube 1980]. The Theravādin interlocutor rejects this contention, arguing that an arahant has completely overcome delusion (*vītamoha*), possesses the Dhamma-eye (*dhammacakkhu*), and realizes liberation directly without being dependent on others (*na paravitāraṇā*) [Dutt 1978; Dube 1980]. Buddhaghosa glosses the term by explaining that opponents consider that others elucidate, reveal, or declare those matters to them (*pare vitaranti pakāsenti ācikkhanti*) [Dutt 1945]. Modern scholars have discussed the translation of *paravitāraṇā*, noting early renderings such as "excelled by others" alongside interpretations of "induced investigation," "comprehension by others," or "bringing across," which align closely with Tibetan (*yongs su brtag pa*) and Chinese (*ta ling ru*) counterparts found in non-Theravāda records [Eckel 2008; Skorupski 1991; Williams 2000; Yao 2005].
SuttaCentral records one translation and notes references connecting the text with the *Dhotakamāṇavapucchā* (Snp 5.6) and sections of the *Mahāniddesa* and *Cūḷaniddesa* [SuttaCentral]. Computational analysis by DharmaNexus highlights extensive Pali-internal text reuse with neighboring Kathāvatthu controversies dealing with the Five Points, notably *Kaṅkhākathā* (Kv 2.3), *Aññāṇakathā* (Kv 2.2), and *Parūpahārakathā* (Kv 2.1), as well as *Parihānikathā* (Kv 1.2) [DharmaNexus]. Outside the *Kathāvatthu*, DharmaNexus registers shared passages with Niddesa commentaries (Cnd 23, Mnd 13) and Saṁyutta Nikāya collections (SN 35, SN 22, SN 56), in addition to cross-language alignments with Sanskrit and Tibetan scriptures, including the *Vajracchedikā* and *Śatasāhasrikā Prajñāpāramitā* [DharmaNexus].
